---
title: "Adding a source"
description: "Wire a new vendor in behind the same --source flag."
---

The StoryGraph matching-and-writing side is source-agnostic. To add a vendor you implement one
small class and register it; everything downstream — matching, edition tagging, the sync store,
ratings — comes for free.

## The `Source` protocol

A source is any class satisfying the `Source` protocol in
[`src/storywell/sources/base.py`](https://github.com/drmowinckels/storywell/blob/main/src/storywell/sources/base.py):

```python
class Source(Protocol):
    name: str
    media_format: str = ""   # "audio" | "ebook" | "print" | "" (mixed/unknown)

    def finished_books(self, *, threshold: float = 0.95) -> list[SourceBook]: ...
```

- **`name`** is what users pass to `--source`.
- **`media_format`** tells the sync which StoryGraph edition to tag. An `audio` source marks the
  audiobook edition; `ebook`/`print` tag the best match; `""` leaves it to per-book resolution.
- **`finished_books()`** returns `SourceBook`s — the normalised shape every source produces (title,
  authors, ISBNs when available, `percent_complete`, `finished_at`, optional rating/review). Apply
  the `threshold` to decide what counts as finished.

## Register it

Add the class to the `SOURCES` table in
[`src/storywell/sources/__init__.py`](https://github.com/drmowinckels/storywell/blob/main/src/storywell/sources/__init__.py):

```python
SOURCES: dict[str, type[Source]] = {
    AudibleSource.name: AudibleSource,
    # ...
    MyVendorSource.name: MyVendorSource,
}
```

That's it — it now appears in `storywell sources` and works under `--source myvendor`.

## Picking up CLI options

`make_source()` inspects your constructor's signature and passes through only the options it
declares, dropping the rest. So one CLI surface can carry the union of every source's options, and
your source opts in to just what it needs:

```python
class MyVendorSource:
    name = "myvendor"
    media_format = "ebook"

    def __init__(self, *, path: Path | None = None):  # picks up --file
        ...
```

The CLI option names map to constructor parameters as: `--file → path`, `--token → token`,
`--auth-file → auth_file`, `--profile → profile`, `--shelf → shelf`, `--as-read → mark_read`,
`--read-date → read_date`, `--collection → collections`. Declare the ones you want; ignore the
others. A library/borrow source that wants its books on a non-`read` shelf accepts `shelf` and
sets each `SourceBook.status` accordingly (a finished signal still wins and routes to `read`).

## Reuse the CSV machinery

If your vendor exports a CSV or TSV, subclass `CsvSource`
([`src/storywell/sources/csv_source.py`](https://github.com/drmowinckels/storywell/blob/main/src/storywell/sources/csv_source.py))
and implement only `row_to_book`. It handles delimiter detection, the finished filter, and ISBN
unwrapping for you — that's how the Goodreads and LibraryThing sources stay small.

## Ship it with tests

Keep the pure parsing/mapping helpers (row → `SourceBook`, finished filter) as standalone functions
so they're unit-testable without touching the network or a device — the existing sources all follow
this `*_from_row` / injectable-transport pattern. New source, new tests, same change.
